FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards after the draft finalized by the Bitumen, Tar 
and Related Products Sectional Committee had been approved by the Petroleum, Coal and Related Product 
Division Council. 


To determine the characteristics of the bitumen in a bitumen paving mixture, it is necessary to extract the bitumen 
from the aggregate by means of a suitable solvent and then to recover the bitumen from the solvent without 
significantly changing the bitumen properties. The bitumen recovered from the solvent by method can be tested 
using the same methods as for the original bitumen and comparisons between the properties of the original and 
recovered bitumen can bemade. It is also used to study the properties of bitumen aged in service. 


When the bitumen is extracted from bituminous mixture by centrifuge method, some ultra-finemineral material 
which passed through the filter may be present in the extract liquid. If the amount of this mineral material is more 
than 1 percent, the properties of bitumen recovered by this method may be affected. In such cases, it is recommended 
to remove the ultra- fine material from the extract liquid by using any suitable high-speed (3000 rpm or higher) 
centrifuge of the continuous flow type. 


Considerable assistance has been drawn from the ASTM D 5404-12 “Standard practice for recovery of asphalt 
from solution using the rotary evaporator” in formulation of this draft standard. 


The composition of the Committee, responsible for formulation of this standard is listed in Annex A. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS 2 : 2022 ‘Rules for rounding off numerical values (second revision)’. The number of significant places retained 
in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 18130 : 2023 


Indian Standard 


METHOD FOR RECOVERY OF BITUMEN FROM SOLUTION 
USING ROTARY EVAPORATOR 


1 SCOPE 


This standard prescribes the method of recovery of 
bitumen from a solution using rotary evaporator 
ensuring that changes in the bitumen properties 
during recovery process are minimized. 


2 REFERENCE 


The following standards contain provisions which, 
through reference in text constitute provisions of this 
standard. At the time of publication, the editions 
indicated were valid. All the standards are subject to 
revision, and parties to agreements based on this 
standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility 
of applying the most recent editions of the standards 
indicated below:

4 PRINCIPLE 


The solution of bitumen and solvent from a prior 
extraction is distilled by partially immersing the 
rotating distillation flask of the rotary evaporator 
in a heated oil bath. The solution is subjected to 
a partial vacuum and a flow of nitrogen gas or 
carbon dioxide gas. These gases provide inert 
atmosphere to prevent oxidation of the bitumen 
during the recovery process. 


NOTE — The quality of the results obtained from this 
standard method are largely dependent on the competence 
of the personnel performing the test and 
calibration/maintenance of the test equipment. 


5 APPARATUS 


5.1 Rotary Evaporator — Equipped with a 
distillation flask, a variable speed motor capable of 
rotating the distillation flask (2 1 capacity) at a rate 
of about 50 rpm, condenser solvent recovery flask, 
and heated oil bath. Angle of the distillation flask 
from the horizontal to the bath is set at about 15° (see 
Fig.1). The distillation flask when fully immersed, 
should be at a depth of about 40 mm.

IS 18130 : 2023 


5.2 Thermometric Device — A built in temperature 
measurement device capable displaying the oil 
temperature to the nearest 1°C. 


5.3 Manometer or vacuum gauge — Suitable for 
measuring the specified vacuum (see cl. 7) 


5.4 Gas flowmeter — Capable of indicating a gas 
flow ofup to 1000 ml/min. 


5.5 Sample container — Having adequate volume 
to hold the sample and added solvent. 


5.6 Vacuum system — Capable of maintaining a 
vacuum to within + 0.7 kPa (+ 5 mm of Hg) of the 
desired level up to and including 80 kPa [600 mm of 


Hg]. 

5.7 Oven — Capable of maintaining a temperature 
of 165 °C +5 °C. 

6 REAGENTS AND MATERIALS 

6.1 Nitrogen Gas or Carbon Dioxide Gas — A 


pressurized tank with pressure-reducing valve, or 
any other convenient source. 


NOTE — Different flow rates may be required whether 
nitrogen gas or carbon dioxide gas is used. 


6.2 Oil — The oil for the heated oil bath should be 
food grade white oil or silicone fluid with flash point 
above 215°C or an equivalent. 


6.3 Solvents — The solvent for extracting the 
bitumen from mixtures should be reagent grade 
trichloroethylene or methylene chloride. It is 
recommended that for each new supply of solvent,a 
blank should be run on a bitumen with known 
properties. 


6.3.1 Precautions 


6.3.1.1 The solvents listed in 6.3 should be used only 
under a hood or with an effective surface exhaust 
system exhaust system in a well-ventilated area, since 
they are toxic to various degrees. 


6.3.1.2 These solvents may be hydrolyzed in the 
presence of heat and moisture to form acids that are 
extremely corrosive to certain metals, especially 
when subject to contact over lengthy periods to time. 
It is necessary to take proper precautions to not allow 
these solvents to remainin small quantities in the 
effluent tanks of aluminum vacuum extractors. 


6.3.1.3 Exposure of these solvents or their vapors to 
high temperature such as contact with flames, hot 
glowing surfaces, or electric arcs can produce 
decomposition products such as hydrogen chloride. 
Steel drums containing these solvents should be 
stored in a cool, dry locations, kept tightly sealed, 
and opened as infrequently as possible. The 
hydrogen chloride in decomposed solvent may 
harden a bitumen during the extraction and recovery 
test and thusgive erroneous test results. 


7 PROCEDURE 


7.1 Heat the oil bath to temperature of 140 *C 
+3°C. Start circulating cold water through 
the condenser. 


72 Apply a vacuum of 5.3 kPa + 0.7 kPa 
[40 mm Hg + 5 mm Hg] below atmospheric 
pressure and draw approximately 600 ml of 
bitumen solution from the sample container into 
the distillation flask through the sample line. Begin 
a nitrogen or carbon dioxide flow of 
approximately 500 ml/min through the system 
(see Note). Begin rotating the distillation flask (at 
approximately 40 rpm) and lower the flask into the 
oil bath. Initially the immersion depth of the flask 
will be determined by the need to achieve a 
controlled solvent evaporation rate. The correct rate 
of evaporation can be observed as steady 
controlled stream of condensed solvent being 
collectedin the recovery flask. 


NOTE — The vacuum and nitrogen or carbon dioxide flow 
values may need to be adjusted depending on thelocation. 
Also, low flow values are recommended at the beginning of 
the rotary process when the sample volume is large because 
of the possibility of back flow into the vacuum system. The 
possibility of back flow can also be minimized by regulating 
the depth of immersion of the flask. 
7.3 When the amount of bitumen solution within the 
distillation flask appears low enough so that more 
solution may be added, discontinue the nitrogen or 
carbon dioxide flow. Draw the remaining bitumen 
solution from the sample container into the 
distillation flask and readjust the nitrogen or carbon 
dioxide flow (see Note). 
NOTE — The equipment may be modified to allow a 
continuous flow of solution from the sample container into 
the distillation flask such that the volume in the distillation 
flask maintained at approximately 600 ml. The nitrogen or 
carbon dioxide flow is not started until all the solution has 
entered the distillation flask. 


7.4 When most of the solvent has been distilled from 
the bitumen and no obvious condensation is 
occurring on the condenser, the flask should be 
immersed to the recommended maximum 
immersion depth of approximately 40 mm. Slowly 
apply a vacuum of 80.0 kPa + 0.7 kPa (600 mm of 
Hg + 5 mm of Hg) below atmospheric pressure. 
Increase nitrogen or carbon dioxide flow to 
approximately 600 ml/min and the spin rate of the 
distillation flask to about 45 rpm. Hold or reduce 
vacuum if foaming or a bubbly formation occurs. 
When foaming subsides apply maximum vacuum. 
Maintain this condition for 10 min + 1 min. 

NOTES 

1 It is recommended that the flask be immersed for up to 2 

min before slowly applying the vacuum. 

2 A faster flask spin rate exposes more surface area of the 

bitumen and, hence, dislodges more traces of solvent from 

the bitumen. The rotation speed of the flask may also be 

varied or flask rotation may be stopped to enhance the 

removal of solvent. 


3 Due to the cooling effect of the increased nitrogen or 
carbon dioxide flow, an increase in the temperature of the 


oil bath is generally needed to maintain a constant sample 
temperature. Experience has shown that a typical oil bath 
temperature range of 150 *C to 155 *C is satisfactory for 
this purpose. 


7.5 At the end of the 15 min period, remove the 
distillation flask from the apparatus and wipethe 
flask to clean the oil. Pour the bitumen into a proper 
size container. If needed, the flask may beinverted 
and placed into an oven at 165 °C + 1 °C for 10 min 


IS 18130 : 2023 


to 15 min to cause the bitumen to flow into the 
container. The bitumen should not be allowed to be 
distributed over the interior of the flask. 


7.6 Portions of the recovered bitumen, while still in 
a liquid state, can be taken for determination of 
properties such as penetration, viscosity, softening 
point, ductility, Complex shear modulus G, and 
angle as required.
